memory_candidates.content: When a plan declares Commit Mode: atomic-batch for a phase whose two edits are interdependent (a write-path change and a count-path change to the same marker), verify both halves together with a single fixture before committing: a positive round-trip AND a negative-fixture end-to-end run of the real gate (not just the regex in isolation). Reverting only one half of an atomic-batch phase should be structurally impossible to reach in a green state, and the negative fixture is what proves the permissive regex change did not also weaken the gate for genuinely incomplete work.

Before executing a plan's fixture verification for a shell-block change embedded in an agent .md file (e.g. Stage 5a's marker-repair loop), extract the code fence verbatim from the deployed file and execute it against a throwaway fixture rather than retyping the logic. This tests the shipped text, not the author's mental model of it, and catches transcription drift immediately (e.g. a byte-identity check across two agent files' embedded blocks is only meaningful if both extractions are exact).

A plan's Scope Hypothesis census can find MORE than what it declared; the plan's own escalate-vs-absorb rule (fix a discovered same-pattern one-line site inline, escalate substantive rewrites to a follow-up note) is the right default for implementers rather than silently ignoring the discovery or silently expanding scope without a rationale. Recording the correction explicitly in the summary keeps the plan's declared scope auditable against what was actually touched.
